title: 3 reasons why you should breath through your nose while training
summary: He recommends always inhaling through the nose. It filters germs, shapes the jaw during growth, lets you keep the jaw clenched for strength, and controls oxygen intake for better stamina. It also retains heat in cold weather.
claims: Always inhale through your nose and exhale through the nose or mouth, in daily life and in training
Nose hair and mucus filter out viruses and germs, lowering your chance of getting sick
Nose breathing keeps the tongue on the roof of the mouth behind the teeth, which shapes the mouth and jaw as you grow; chronic mouth-breathing kids develop different facial structure
Nose breathing lets you keep your jaw clenched while lifting; an open mouth is a strength vacuum, try a deadlift with a slack jaw
Olympic lifters open their mouths because their lifts have no negative phase
Strongmen use mouthguards so they can bite down and keep the jaw tight
Nose breathing lets you control oxygen intake precisely, so heart and lungs work more efficiently and stamina increases
Coaches used to punish him for mouth breathing with 15 push-ups
In cold climates nose breathing retains moisture and body heat and warms incoming air
